newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Welteke says hopes no early U.S. rate rise.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Welteke says hopes no early U.S. rate rise.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Ernst Welteke said on Tuesday that he hoped U.S. interest rates would remain steady for as long as possible, adding that an increase in rates there could push German rates higher.

"I can only hope that interest rates in the U.S. remain stable for as long as possible and are not raised, as this could, under certain circumstances, mean that rates here would go higher as well, which cannot be desirable in current conditions," Welteke was quoted as saying by a German radio.

According to a statement on the contents of the interview, Welteke added that the Bundesbank considered the current level of German interest rates appropriate in view of current inflation, the economic situation and M3 money supply growth.
M3 is the Bundesbank's main monetary policy indicator, but the central bank also watches a wide range of other statistics.
Germany's discount rate, the floor for money market rates, is currently at a record low of 2.50 percent.
